name: Fast-DetectGPT Probability Curvature
description: A high-speed, zero-shot detection algorithm that identifies AI-generated text by analyzing the conditional probability curvature of words without needing expensive text perturbations.
algorithm: Conditional Probability Curvature Estimation (Bao et al., 2024)
mechanism: DetectGPT proved that AI-generated text sits at the absolute peak (local maxima) of a model's log-probability curve. If you change a few words (perturbation), the probability drops drastically. Human text, however, sits in the random valleys of this curve, so changing words doesn't drastically lower the probability. The original DetectGPT was painfully slow because it required generating hundreds of variations of the text to map this curve. Fast-DetectGPT is a mathematical breakthrough. Instead of generating hundreds of fake variations, it analytically computes the conditional probability of each token and uses a surrogate scoring function to estimate the probability curvature in a single pass. It measures how much the current word's probability diverges from the expected probability of all other possible words in that exact context. If the text consistently hits the sharpest mathematical peaks of conditional probability space—meaning the words chosen are always the hyper-optimal, safest choices—it triggers the algorithmic detection threshold instantly.
useCase: The ultimate workhorse for detecting raw, unaltered AI text in real-time. Ideal for scanning massive volumes of text where computational efficiency and zero-shot accuracy are required.
strengths:
• Blisteringly fast compared to original DetectGPT (up to 340x faster) while maintaining or exceeding its detection accuracy.
• Zero-shot capability: It does not need to be trained on the specific AI model that generated the text to catch it.
• Mathematically rigorous; it doesn't look at grammar or style, but directly interrogates the fundamental autoregressive nature of LLMs.
limitations:
• Susceptible to heavy adversarial paraphrasing (like WordAI or aggressive QuillBot), which artificially lowers the probability peaks to mimic human valleys.
• Accuracy degrades on extremely short texts (under 100 words) because there aren't enough tokens to calculate a reliable curvature map.
• Inherently struggles with heavily constrained human writing (e.g., highly technical manuals or code) which naturally exists at higher probability peaks.
parameters:
Analysis: Single-Pass Conditional Probability & Surrogate Scoring
Metric: Estimated Log-Probability Curvature Deviance
Output: 0-100 Probability Curvature (Algorithmic Maxima) Score
accuracy: Very High — 85-95% on unmodified AI text of sufficient length. It is currently one of the most efficient stat-of-the-art diagnostic tools in AI forensics.

references.title: Bao, G. et al. (2024). Fast-DetectGPT: Efficient Zero-Shot Detection of Machine-Generated Text via Conditional Probability Curvature. ICLR.
Mitchell, E. et al. (2023). DetectGPT: Zero-Shot Machine-Generated Text Detection using Probability Curvature. ICML.
